name: Garba v University of Maiduguri
summary: A foundational fair-hearing case on disciplinary proceedings in a university setting and the requirements of natural justice.
facts: Students were subjected to university disciplinary measures arising from campus disturbances. They challenged the process as denying them a fair hearing.
issues: Whether the disciplinary process met the constitutional and common-law requirements of fair hearing.
What procedural protections apply before serious disciplinary sanctions.
holding: The decision emphasises that bodies exercising disciplinary powers must observe fair hearing / natural justice. Read the full report for the precise findings on the university process in issue.
ratio: Where a decision affects rights or serious interests, the decision-maker must afford a fair opportunity to be heard; failure of natural justice can invalidate the resulting decision.
report_citation: See NWLR / law-report citation via a licensed law-report service

interpretations.body: Map the case onto Constitution s.36(1): fair hearing within a reasonable time by an independent and impartial body. Distinguish between academic/administrative discipline and criminal prosecution, but note that fairness still binds both.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
